title: Petrobras Stock After Q3 Earnings - Buy, Sell or Hold for Now? - The Globe and Mail
content: Brazil's state-run energy giant Petroleo Brasileiro S.A., better known as PetrobrasPBR, not only produced more oil and gas but also earned more than a year earlier in the third quarter of 2026. It also raised its annual production and cash-flow forecasts. Those are good reasons to look at the stock, even after its sharp rise this year. There are reasons for caution, too, as profit declined from the second quarter, while spending increased. For investors wondering whether to buy, the question is how much of the expected improvement is already priced in. Petrobras reported revenues of $33 billion, up 40.4% from a year earlier. Profit attributable to shareholders rose 28.4% to $7.7 billion. Excluding one-off items, profit increased 78% to $9.3 billion. Operating cash flow reached $12 billion, up 22%, while free cash flow rose 33.2% to $6.6 billion. Free cash flow measures what remains after investment spending. The stock has already rewarded investors. PBR shares have gained 54.8% in 2026 compared with 41.8% for ExxonMobil HoldingsXOM and 44.3% for ChevronCVX. A large gain alone does not tell us whether a stock is expensive, but it makes the earnings outlook worth examining closely. The results were weaker than the second quarter. Reported shareholder profit fell 25.8%, while profit excluding one-off items declined 15.9%. Lower oil prices hurt earnings, as did higher expenses. Investors should keep that comparison in mind when assessing the much stronger annual numbers. Petrobras produced a record 3.512 million barrels of oil equivalent per day (MMBOE/d) during the quarter. Refineries ran at 99% of capacity, and diesel production reached a record 769,000 barrels daily. Management now expects annual production of 3.3–3.4 MMBOE/d, up from 3.1 million. Offshore platforms are reaching higher output sooner, and the P-79 platform started earlier than planned. Petrobras also raised its operating cash-flow forecast to $45-$50 billion from $35 billion. That forecast uses higher production and revised oil-price assumptions, so the increase does not come entirely from operating improvements. ExxonMobil reported production growth in Guyana and the Permian, excluding Middle East effects, while Chevron increased capacity at existing facilities. For Petrobras, the same basic test applies: does spending lead to more production and enough cash to justify the cost? Fourth-quarter production faces scheduled maintenance and a lower Petrobras share of output under the Búzios production-sharing agreement. Investors should not assume production will rise every quarter. The Zacks Consensus Estimate for Petrobras’ 2026 earnings is $4.95 per share, up 76.8% from $2.80 in 2025. That expected increase gives the share-price rally some support. The forecast still depends on production, costs and oil prices, and it should be treated as an expectation rather than money already earned. PBR trades at a lower forward price-to-earnings ratio than its industry, ExxonMobil and Chevron. Put simply, investors pay less for each dollar of Petrobras’ expected earnings. That makes the stock worth considering after its rally. The discount needs context. Petrobras is state-controlled, which creates a risk that government priorities influence business decisions. A cheaper earnings multiple is attractive only if investors are comfortable with those risks and the earnings used to calculate it. Petrobras raised its annual cash investment forecast to $21-$22 billion from $16.9 billion. Its manageable operating expense forecast increased to $24.2–$25.5 billion from $20.2 billion. Management nevertheless expects those expenses per barrel to fall 2% from 2025. Higher lease payments also use cash. Investors comparing Petrobras with ExxonMobil and Chevron should consider how much remains for shareholders after investment and other commitments. Net debt fell to $57.8 billion. Fitch raised Petrobras’ standalone credit profile to bbb+, although its global rating remained BB. The Amapá discovery may offer future resources, but commercial development is uncertain. The agreement to buy the remaining Logum stake also awaits approvals, and its logistics benefits are expected ahead. PBR looks like a buy for investors willing to accept oil-price swings and the risks of state control. Higher production and expected earnings growth support that view, while the valuation remains below peers despite the rally. Rising spending deserves attention because higher operating cash flow does not automatically mean more money for shareholders. On balance, the price and earnings outlook favor buying over selling or waiting. Petrobras stock is currently a Zacks Rank #2 (Buy). SPRING, Texas--(BUSINESS WIRE)--
ExxonMobil Holdings Corporation ("ExxonMobil") (NYSE: XOM) today announces that its wholly owned subsidiaries Pioneer Natural Resources Company ("Pioneer") and Exxon Mobil Corporation ("Exxon" and, together with Pioneer, the "Offerors" and each, an "Offeror"), have commenced cash tender offers (each, a "Tender Offer" and collectively, the "Tender Offers") to purchase up to $3,000,000,000 aggregate principal amount (the "Maximum Waterfall Tender Amount") of the following series of notes (collectively, the "Notes"): (i) Pioneer’s 1.900% Senior Notes due 2030 (the "2030 Pioneer Notes") and 2.150% Senior Notes due 2031 (the "2031 Pioneer Notes" and, together with the 2030 Pioneer Notes, the "Pioneer Notes"); and (ii) Exxon’s 3.482% Notes due 2030 (the "2030 Exxon Notes") and 4.227% Notes due 2040 (the "2040 Exxon Notes" and, together with the 2030 Exxon Notes, the "Exxon Notes"). Pioneer is offering to purchase only the Pioneer Notes, and Exxon is offering to purchase only the Exxon Notes. Holders will receive a price equal to the Total Consideration based on the applicable Reference Yield and the applicable Fixed Spread plus Accrued Interest (each as defined below). Each Tender Offer is being made upon the terms and subject to the conditions set forth in the Offer to Purchase dated November 16, 2026 (the "Offer to Purchase"). Terms not defined in this announcement have the meanings given to them in the Offer to Purchase. The Offerors are offering to purchase the Notes for cash up to the Maximum Waterfall Tender Amount in aggregate principal amount. Subject to the Maximum Waterfall Tender Amount, the amount of a series of Notes that is purchased in the Tender Offers will be based on the order of priority (the "Acceptance Priority Level") for such series, as set forth in the table below. Notes of a series may be subject to proration if the aggregate principal amount of the Notes of such series validly tendered would cause the Maximum Waterfall Tender Amount to be exceeded. The Maximum Waterfall Tender Amount applies to the Pioneer Notes and the Exxon Notes in the aggregate. The Offerors, acting jointly, reserve the right, but are not obligated, to increase or decrease the Maximum Waterfall Tender Amount, in their sole and absolute discretion, subject to applicable law. Notes purchased in the Tender Offers will be cancelled. No Tender Offer is conditioned on any minimum principal amount of Notes being tendered. The consummation of each Tender Offer is subject to, and conditioned upon, the satisfaction or waiver, where permitted, of the conditions discussed in the Offer to Purchase. Subject to the satisfaction or waiver by the Offerors of the conditions of each Tender Offer described in the Offer to Purchase and subject to the Maximum Waterfall Tender Amount, the Offerors will accept Notes for purchase in the order of their respective Acceptance Priority Level specified in this table, with 1 being the highest Acceptance Priority Level and 4 being the lowest Acceptance Priority Level. The "Total Consideration" per $1,000 principal amount of Notes of each series validly tendered at or prior to the applicable Expiration Date and not validly withdrawn and accepted for purchase will be calculated as described in the Offer to Purchase using the applicable Fixed Spread. See "Description of the Tender Offers—Total Consideration" in the Offer to Purchase. The Total Consideration does not include accrued and unpaid interest on such Notes from the last interest payment date with respect to such Notes to, but not including, the Settlement Date (the "Accrued Interest"), which will be paid in addition to the Total Consideration. Each Tender Offer will expire at 5:00 p.m., New York City time, on November 20, 2026, unless extended or earlier terminated (such date and time, as the same may be extended or earlier terminated, the "Expiration Date"). Holders who desire to participate in any Tender Offer must validly tender their Notes at or prior to the applicable Expiration Date. Tenders of Notes may be validly withdrawn at any time on or prior to the applicable Expiration Date but tenders will thereafter be irrevocable, except in certain limited circumstances where additional withdrawal rights are required by law. In the event proration is required, the applicable Offeror will multiply the principal amount of each valid tender of such series of Notes by the applicable proration factor and make appropriate downward adjustments to avoid purchases of Notes in principal amounts other than an Authorized Denomination, in order to determine the principal amount of such tender that will be accepted pursuant to the applicable Tender Offer. Upon the terms and subject to the conditions set forth in the Offer to Purchase, holders of the Notes ("Holders") who validly tender and who do not validly withdraw Notes at or prior to the applicable Expiration Date and whose Notes are accepted for purchase by the applicable Offeror (subject to the applicable Acceptance Priority Levels and to proration, if any) will receive the Total Consideration, plus Accrued Interest. The Total Consideration payable for the Notes will be a price per $1,000 principal amount of Notes, calculated with reference to the Settlement Date, that would reflect a yield to the applicable maturity date or par call date, as applicable, of such Notes equal to the sum of (i) the applicable Reference Yield determined at the Price Determination Time, plus (ii) the applicable Fixed Spread. The Total Consideration payable for each of the 2030 Pioneer Notes, the 2031 Pioneer Notes, the 2030 Exxon Notes and the 2040 Exxon Notes will be determined as set out in the calculation in Schedule A to the Offer to Purchase. title: Exxon Mobil Earnings Call Highlights Growth and Resilience - The Globe and Mail
content: Exxon Mobil Corp. ((XOM)) has held its Q3 earnings call. Read on for the main highlights of the call. Exxon Mobil delivered a strongly positive earnings call, highlighting record operating performance, robust cash generation, production growth and a stronger balance sheet. Management also pointed to major shareholder returns, cost savings and project progress, while acknowledging Middle East disruptions, refining uncertainty and execution challenges. ExxonMobil reported $15.4 billion in GAAP earnings and $25.7 billion in operating cash flow for the third quarter. The results underscored the company’s ability to generate substantial cash across its integrated oil, gas, refining and chemicals businesses. The company invested $7 billion in its business and returned $9.4 billion to shareholders through dividends and share repurchases. ExxonMobil also raised its dividend per share by 4%, extending its record of annual increases to 44 consecutive years. ExxonMobil reduced net debt by more than $9 billion during the quarter. Management said net debt relative to capital was the strongest in the industry, apart from possibly one large-cap industrial company. ExxonMobil processes about 3.6 million barrels of crude daily and sells roughly 5.7 million barrels of finished products worldwide. Gulf Coast refineries operated at about 100% crude-unit utilization, while overall utilization was approximately 84%. Diesel yield was about 3.5% higher than in 2019, adding an estimated $1.5 billion to quarterly margins and $3.5 billion year to date. Since 2019, Energy Products earnings per barrel have tripled on a constant-price-and-margin basis, supported by better product mix and lower structural costs. Asset-reconfiguration projects on the U.S. Gulf Coast are expected to increase distillate output by about 100,000 barrels per day. The first phase is underway at Baytown, with further projects planned to improve diesel, lubricant and chemical-feedstock yields at existing sites. ExxonMobil said it has invested more than $200 billion over the past decade. Structural savings since 2019 have reached $16.9 billion, keeping the company on track for $20 billion in cumulative savings by 2030. Excluding Middle East effects, production increased from a year earlier. Continued growth in the Permian Basin and Guyana remained the main drivers of the upstream performance. Production from the Stabroek Block in Guyana has exceeded 1 billion barrels, just 11 years after discovery. ExxonMobil said its fifth development, Uaru, is expected to begin production in the fourth quarter. Cumulative LNG production in Papua New Guinea has surpassed 100 million tons, while the Papua LNG project is positioned for further growth after ExxonMobil increased its working interest and assumed operatorship. In Mozambique, an agreement with Eni will raise ExxonMobil’s operated interest in Rovuma LNG to 50%. ExxonMobil received approval for the Rose Carbon Storage Project and began carbon-capture operations for Nucor. The company said its CCS business now has 11 million metric tons per annum under contract across eight customers. ExxonMobil said it has reduced methane intensity by more than 60% since 2016. The company also received Gold Standard recognition from the United Nations’ Oil and Gas Methane Partnership. Three automated drilling rigs are operating in the Permian and are improving safety and performance, according to management. ExxonMobil expects automated units to account for about 25% of its Permian fleet next year and roughly half by 2028. The Permian program has reached its year-end production guidance ahead of schedule. Management said secondary-recovery technologies offer a path toward significantly higher recovery, although the more meaningful benefits are expected beyond 2030. Trading and optimization volumes are now four times their 2019 level. ExxonMobil said its teams secured feedstocks, redirected supplies and moved products to higher-value markets as conditions changed. Golden Pass Train 1 advanced after ExxonMobil took over work from a bankrupt contractor. Train 2 was expected to be substantially complete by December, while mechanical completion for Train 3 was expected in mid-2027. Management highlighted a broad project pipeline that could contribute beyond 2030. Exploration spending has averaged about $1 billion annually over the past five years, with discoveries in Guyana, Angola and Cyprus, while Product Solutions opportunities include diesel, graphite materials and Proxxima systems. Expected annual synergies from the Pioneer acquisition have increased from $2 billion to $4 billion. ExxonMobil also said its Global Projects organization is executing twice as many mega-projects as international oil company peers, at 20% lower cost and 20% faster scheduled time. ExxonMobil continues working with partners and Mozambique’s government toward a final investment decision for Rovuma LNG. Management said combining the upstream and downstream portions could improve capital efficiency, although the potential benefit has not been quantified. The European Parliament voted to delay implementation of the EU Methane Regulation by three years. ExxonMobil said the additional time should help the industry build compliance systems after the required implementation steps are defined. The continuing Middle East conflict has disrupted trade flows and constrained supplies of crude, diesel, gasoline and other products. Those disruptions have contributed to tighter markets and higher prices. ExxonMobil maintained its estimate of a 350,000-barrel-per-day impact in the fourth quarter, concentrated largely in Qatar LNG after facility damage and lost trains. UAE production was near historical levels, but logistics constraints delayed sales and limited the movement of barrels. Management estimated that about one-third of the global product shortage was linked to difficulties moving clean products out of the Middle East. It also estimated that roughly half of Russia’s refining capacity was offline, turning the country from a net exporter into a net importer of clean products. Management said a return to balance depends on the reopening of the Strait of Hormuz, an end to attacks on regional refining facilities and repairs to damaged plants. China’s export levels will also matter, and normalization could take well through next year or longer. The bankruptcy of a contractor created difficulties at Golden Pass and required ExxonMobil to take over the work. The company is progressing with remaining contractors and QatarEnergy. ExxonMobil described Venezuela’s resources as difficult to develop because of crude quality and production challenges. Management said fiscal and legal frameworks, along with investor protections, still need major changes before the company would consider committing significant resources. Historical project structures in Kazakhstan have created complexity and limited effective resource development. ExxonMobil is working with partners and the government on a revised proposal, but discussions remain ongoing and could take time. ExxonMobil called the original EU Methane Regulation timetable unworkable because the compliance deadline preceded the rules needed to implement it. The company said it would have stopped importing into Europe without a workable compliance path. ExxonMobil does not plan to hold a formal corporate plan update in December, unlike in recent years. Instead, it expects to reaffirm key 2027 planning metrics in a press release and provide more detail with fourth-quarter results. ExxonMobil expects Uaru to start in the fourth quarter, Gulf Coast projects to add about 100,000 barrels per day of distillate yield and automated rigs to reach half of the Permian fleet by 2028. The company also targets $20 billion in cumulative savings by 2030 and plans $20 billion of share repurchases in 2027, assuming reasonable market conditions. The company expects Golden Pass Train 2 to be substantially complete by December and Train 3 to reach mechanical completion in mid-2027. Rovuma LNG is still targeted for a final investment decision by year-end, while refining disruptions may persist through next year or longer and the Middle East is expected to reduce fourth-quarter output by 350,000 barrels per day. ExxonMobil’s call presented a company with strong earnings, cash flow and financial flexibility, supported by production growth and disciplined investment. However, Middle East disruptions, refining uncertainty and complex international projects remain important risks for investors to monitor. © Copyright 2026 The Globe and Mail Inc.
